messages.subject: Re: jitter/dodge y values
parts:
Hi,

This is nothing fancy, but you could do something like:

tmp <- factor(dat$V4)
dat$jiteredY <- ave(as.numeric(tmp), tmp, FUN = function(x) x +
rnorm(length(x), sd = .05))

ggplot(dat, aes(x = V1, y = jitteredY, xend = V2, yend = jitteredY,
colour = V3)) +
geom_segment()

Cheers,

Josh

On Tue, Jun 21, 2011 at 3:46 PM, Zev <jew...@gmail.com> wrote:
> Joshua FTW.
>
> I jumped the gun.  Your code works perfectly!

I am glad my code ended up working out :) To be honest, I am a little
surprised that yours did not work. jittering seems to work at least
with a little example I cooked up, but I could not come up with what I
was doing differently than you, which is why I gave the alternate
solution of manually jittering the y values. Out of curiosity, do you
get jittering using the code below? I attached, what I get.


require(ggplot2)
## some plots using the built in "iris" dataset
plotnorm <- ggplot(iris, aes(x = Petal.Length, xend = Petal.Width,
y = factor(Species), yend = factor(Species))) +
geom_segment(position = "identity") +
opts(title = "Normal segments")

plotjit <- ggplot(iris, aes(x = Petal.Length, xend = Petal.Width,
y = factor(Species), yend = factor(Species))) +
geom_segment(position = position_jitter(height = .25)) +
opts(title = "Jittered segments")

pushViewport(vpList(
viewport(x = 0, y = 0, width = .5, height = 1,
just = c("left", "bottom"), name = "normal"),
viewport(x = .5, y = 0, width = .5, height = 1,
just = c("left", "bottom"), name = "jittered")))

print(plotjit, newpage = FALSE)
upViewport()
downViewport("normal")
print(plotnorm, newpage = FALSE)
